tagline: Coding agents treat documents as memory. Doc Governor decides which memories they are allowed to trust.
one_line: Doc Governor repairs the documents code changes affect, then decides which documents an AI coding agent is allowed to believe.
description:
## The problem
Coding agents can turn outdated documentation into confident mistakes. Repairs, verification, and later reads are often disconnected.

## What Doc Governor does
Doc Governor connects three moments: before commit, during pull-request review, and whenever a coding agent requests a document through MCP.

A deterministic Git dependency scan identifies affected documents. A read-only Strands Repair Planner on Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Nova Lite) inspects only its assigned document and changed declared dependencies, then returns a bounded plan. A configured coding-agent executor edits allowlisted documents in an isolated repository; verification and source/index integrity checks must pass before publication.

A separate read-only coding-agent session can review explicitly delegated contracts against sources, tests, and deployment evidence. Repair is not approval. Matching receipts, citations, authorization, and snapshot hashes are required, and changed evidence or revoked authorization invalidates the receipt.

The read-only MCP server checks stored usability, document and dependency hashes, and delegated review authorization. A refused get_document response contains no document body.

## Why Professional Agents
Doc Governor removes repetitive documentation maintenance from a developer's commit-and-review routine while keeping consequential decisions with a person.

## Testing
The public fixture needs no AWS credentials and uses synthetic data. `python scripts/demo.py --mcp-stdio` repairs the affected documents, refuses the unsupported ones through the real MCP stdio server, and prints zero served characters for every refusal. 269 unit tests cover the Strands graph, scoped tools, structured output, and budget hooks with a test model in place of the Bedrock network call.

A separate isolated live run is recorded in `submission/background-schema-live-run-20260908.json`: no model doubles, an 89-second worker publish, an independent read-only reviewer session with its own receipt, and a second agent that read the repaired document back through MCP and answered from it.

## Limits
The Catalog is owner-maintained and every dependency must be declared. Advisor drift checks detect symptomatic signals rather than every possible configuration change. Trust is evidence-bound: it records that a claim still matches the source it cites, not that the prose is true. Doc Governor does not deploy, hold a production write credential, or stop a client from bypassing the read gate with another filesystem tool.

## Reproduce
Install from the public repository following README.md, run `python scripts/demo.py --mcp-stdio` for the credential-free fixture, or run `AWS_PROFILE=docgov-local AWS_REGION=us-west-2 python scripts/background_demo.py --live --output /tmp/docgov-live-schema` for the isolated live-model demonstration.
source_disclosure: Doc Governor began as a deterministic iteration in the public SophieYu04/doc-governor repository; this submission builds on that work rather than claiming every component was independently rewritten. Git history retained in the submitted repository records development beginning September 5, 2026. Strands planning/governance, isolated coding-agent repair, independent trust receipts, MCP enforcement, and AWS integration are included in the submitted history. The public fixture uses synthetic data and contains no private source, credentials, production data, or deployment artifacts. Standard Python, Strands, AWS, MCP, GitHub tooling and AI coding assistants were used. Eligibility is determined by the organizers; commit dates alone do not establish originality.
